one_liner: Ecwid offers a REST API for ecommerce stores using OAuth2 and API keys for app authentication.
gating_notes: Developers create apps in the Ecwid admin to get client_id/secret and access tokens; no explicit free sandbox mentioned, but self-serve app creation is available.
oauth_details: OAuth2 flow implied by client_id/client_secret and access tokens (secret_token/public_token).

auth_methods.quote: Every application has two API keys: `client_id` (app ID) and `client_secret` (app secret). ... Secure app credentials for authorizing REST API requests. If an app is installed in several Ecwid stores, it has unique access tokens for every store. There are two tokens: `secret_token` and `public_token`.

primary_auth.quote: Every application has two API keys: `client_id` (app ID) and `client_secret` (app secret).

credential_access.quote: Hidden page in Ecwid admin where developers can create new applications, check app settings, get access tokens, and request application updates.

api_type.quote: Base URL: `https://app.ecwid.com/api/v3/{storeId}` Full list of endpoints and calls below.

api_breadth.quote: Store profile, checkout extra fields, shipping options, payment options ... Store stats, deleted items history, store reports ... Orders ... Abandoned carts ... Product reviews

pass_history.why: Ecwid uses API key and bearer token, not OAuth2.
Primary auth is API key, not OAuth2.
